transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess the main reason I came in is that I’ve been having a hard time shaking this feeling — more than a feeling, honestly — that certain people around here, like in the arts scene and some finance circles in Cincinnati, are paying attention to me in a way that doesn’t seem normal.

I work with clients, and I’ll notice things like… who knows who I met with, or what event I was invited to, or the topic of a panel discussion suddenly lining up with something I’d just talked about privately. Or I’ll go to an event and someone is seated near me who feels very intentionally placed there. And I know how that sounds — I do. I’ll tell myself, “Okay, maybe this is coincidence, maybe you’re just connecting dots that aren’t connected,” but then it keeps happening, and I can’t really let it go.

It’s been taking up a lot of space in my head, trying to figure out whether people are tracking which clients I meet with and sending little signals through invitations or seating arrangements or event topics. I’m not saying I have proof in a normal, concrete way, but it feels organized enough that it’s hard to dismiss. That’s what finally made me think I should talk to someone.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is actually there?

I don’t think so. I mean, not in the way people usually mean that, like hearing an actual voice in the room when nobody’s there. I haven’t had that, at least not that I’ve recognized.

Sometimes I’ll replay conversations in my head a lot, or I’ll wonder what someone meant by something they said, but that’s more like my own thoughts going over it again and again. It doesn’t feel like a separate voice talking to me. So… no, I don’t think I’ve been hearing voices.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high, energized, or irritable for days at a time?

I’m not sure I’d say that, no. I mean, I have days where I’m more keyed up or irritated than usual, especially if I’m stressed or if something is bothering me and I can’t quite let it go, but I don’t think I’ve had stretches where I’m unusually high or energized for days in the way you might mean.

I haven’t had, like, a period where I suddenly felt amazing and unstoppable or anything like that. And I don’t think I’ve been going for days with tons of extra energy. Irritable, maybe sometimes, but it feels more like normal frustration or tension than some big mood shift. So… I guess my answer is probably no, not really.
When you try to consider the possibility that these patterns are just coincidences, does that feel genuinely possible to you?

I can say it to myself, like, “Maybe this is all coincidence,” and I do try to hold onto that for a minute. I’m not completely unwilling to consider it. But honestly, it doesn’t feel very believable once I start thinking through the specifics.

Because it isn’t just one thing. It’s not just, you know, one panel topic that happens to overlap with a conversation I had, or one person sitting near me at an event. It’s the way it repeats across these arts and finance circles here, where I’ll meet with a client or talk about something privately, and then suddenly an invitation comes through that seems to echo it, or the subject of a discussion lines up too closely, or someone connected to that world ends up near me in a way that feels arranged.

So, genuinely possible? I guess in a technical sense, yes, I know coincidences happen. But emotionally, or practically, it’s hard for me to accept that’s all it is. It feels too organized. Even when I try to talk myself down, I end up back at, “No, someone is tracking this somehow, or people are signaling something.” I don’t have the kind of proof where I could lay it out on a spreadsheet and convince someone else, but I also can’t really let it go.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve felt weighed down at times, and I can get kind of stuck in my head, but I wouldn’t describe it as being depressed most of the day nearly every day.

It’s more like… certain days feel heavier than others, especially if I’ve been thinking a lot or feeling uncertain about things, but it’s not this constant low mood from morning to night. I still have stretches where I’m functioning and talking to people and doing what I need to do. So if you mean a persistent, almost daily depression, I don’t think that’s really what’s been happening.
How long have you been having this sense that people are tracking you or sending you signals?

I’d say about two months. Not years or anything like that. It started feeling noticeable maybe a couple of months ago, where I began to get this sense that things connected to my client meetings were somehow showing up afterward, or that people were kind of signaling around them.

At first I tried to brush it off, because one odd coincidence doesn’t necessarily mean anything. But over those two months it’s kept happening enough that it became harder for me to ignore. So… yes, roughly two months that I’ve had that feeling people may be tracking what I’m doing or sending me messages in some indirect way.
Do you have repetitive unwanted thoughts that you recognize as coming from your own mind and that feel intrusive or hard to resist?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way, exactly. I mean, I do get caught on thoughts, and I’ll go over things in my head more than I probably should, but “repetitive unwanted thoughts” makes me think of something more like a phrase or image that keeps forcing itself in, and I don’t know that that’s what I’m experiencing.

The part about recognizing them as coming from my own mind is also… I don’t know. Some thoughts feel like me worrying or trying to make sense of things, and then other times it feels less like some random intrusive thought and more like I’m responding to something that’s actually happening around me. So I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean thoughts that I clearly know are just internal and irrational but can’t resist. That doesn’t really fit neatly.

I guess the closest I can say is I do think about things repeatedly, and it’s hard to drop them once they feel important. But I don’t experience it as, like, an unwanted mental tic or something I can simply label as “just my mind” and push away.
Have you found yourself losing interest in people or activities you used to care about?

Yeah… I think so, at least somewhat. I wouldn’t say I’ve completely stopped caring about everything, because I still do what I’m supposed to do most of the time, especially with work. But it feels more like I’m getting things done in pieces, like I’ll handle the urgent thing and then sort of stall out on the next step.

For example, client follow-ups that I normally would’ve just knocked out right away will sit there longer than they should. It’s not that I don’t understand they matter. I do. It just feels like there’s less… drive behind it, I guess. Less spark.

And outside of work, yeah, I’ve been skipping things I used to really look forward to. I used to go to jazz nights sometimes, or play pickup basketball, and lately I’ll just not go, and the strange part is I don’t feel that bothered about missing it. It’s more like, “Okay, I didn’t go,” and then I just move on.

Friends have noticed a little, I think. When they ask what’s going on, I usually give short answers, not because I’m mad at them or anything, but because talking feels like more effort than it should. Like even explaining myself feels tiring. So yes, I guess I have lost some interest, or at least I’m not connecting with people and activities the way I used to.
Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from topic to topic in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?

I don’t think anyone has said it to me that directly, no. Like, no one has pulled me aside and said, “You’re not making sense,” or “You’re jumping all over the place.” At least not in those words.

Sometimes I’ll notice people pause or ask me to repeat what I mean, especially if I’m trying to explain something with a lot of moving parts, but I’ve always been kind of detailed when I talk. In my work, I’m used to giving background and context, because if you leave out one piece, the whole thing can sound different. So I might circle around a point more than some people would like, but I don’t know that it’s been hard to follow in a strange way.

I guess my answer is… not really, or not that I’ve noticed. If people think that, they haven’t told me clearly.
During this two-month period, has this sense that people are tracking you been present on most days?

Yeah… most days, I’d say. It hasn’t been every single minute or anything, but the sense of it has been around pretty consistently.

It’s been about two months now that I’ve had this feeling that people are tracking my client meetings, or at least paying attention to them in some organized way. And then there are these moments where something someone says or does feels like a signal connected to that. Some days it’s stronger than others, but it hasn’t really gone away for more than maybe a short stretch. So if you mean during that two-month period, was it there on most days, then… yes, I think that’s fair to say.
Since this started, has your ability to function at work or in daily life clearly gotten worse?

Yeah… I think it has, but not in a dramatic way like I stopped showing up or anything. I’m still working. I still have clients, I still take meetings, I still handle the basics. But if I’m being honest, my practice has gotten smaller than it was.

Some of that is because I’m missing follow-ups, or delaying them long enough that the momentum kind of dies. Like normally, after a meeting, I’d send the summary, check in about paperwork, schedule the next conversation, keep that relationship warm. And lately those things are slipping. Not always, but enough that I can see the difference.

I’ve also been avoiding some public-facing stuff, like panels or events where I’d normally talk to potential clients or be visible. I used to do those because they helped bring people in, and I was comfortable enough with it. Now I find reasons not to go, or I’ll tell myself it’s not worth the time, but I think it’s more than that.

So daily life… I mean, I’m functioning. I pay bills, I get dressed, I go to work. But at work especially, I’m not keeping up the same level of contact with clients that I used to manage. It’s not falling apart, but it’s clearly worse than before.
Have you noticed your emotions feeling flatter than usual, like your face or voice shows less feeling even when something matters to you?

Yeah… I think maybe a little. I don’t know if I would have described it as my face being “flat” exactly, because I’m not watching myself from the outside, but I’ve noticed I don’t have the same kind of spark I usually do.

Like, I still get things done, but it’s in pieces. I’ll do the necessary part of a client thing, then leave the follow-up sitting there even when I know it matters. And it’s not always panic or anything dramatic — sometimes it’s just like I can’t find the push to care in the normal way. The email is right there, I know what I need to say, and I just… don’t.

Outside work, too, I’ve skipped jazz nights I normally like, and pickup basketball, and it doesn’t even bother me as much as it should. Before, if I missed those things, I’d feel like I was missing out or letting the week get away from me. Now it’s more like, “Okay, I’m not going,” and there’s not much feeling attached to it.

And with friends, when they ask what’s going on, I give these short answers. Not because I’m trying to be rude, exactly. It’s more like talking takes more effort than it should, even if the person matters to me. So… yeah, I guess my voice or expression might come across less animated. I haven’t had a lot of people tell me that directly, but from the inside it feels like there’s less there to show.
Have you had the experience that certain thoughts in your mind do not feel like your own?

I don’t think so… not in that exact way.

I mean, I have thoughts I don’t like, or thoughts that feel intrusive in the normal sense, like worries that pop in and I wish they wouldn’t. But they still feel like they’re coming from me, if that makes sense. I don’t have the experience of, like, a thought showing up and feeling clearly foreign or like it was put there by someone else.

Sometimes I’ll second-guess myself a lot, and then I can get stuck trying to figure out why I thought something or what it means. But it still feels like my mind doing it, even if it’s uncomfortable or distracting. So if you mean thoughts that don’t feel like mine at all… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have these experiences been going on for at least three months?

No… not quite three months, I don’t think. It feels longer in my head because I’ve been turning it over so much, but if I’m being careful with the timing, the part where I started really believing people might be tracking my client meetings and sort of sending me signals has been more like two months.

There may have been little things before that where I felt uneasy or wondered if something was off, but the actual pattern — me connecting meetings, messages, little coincidences, and feeling like it meant people were watching or communicating something — that’s been about two months. So I wouldn’t say three months yet, no.
Have you felt that outside forces were controlling your actions or movements?

No… I don’t think it’s like my body is being controlled, if that’s what you mean. I don’t feel like someone is moving my arms or making me walk somewhere against my will.

What brought me in is more… it’s more about feeling like certain people are tracking me, or tracking who I meet with. Like people in these arts and finance circles around Cincinnati — people who overlap in those charity events, gallery things, panels, networking stuff — it feels like they know which clients I’ve been meeting with, and then they sort of send these little signals afterward.

Not controlling my movements exactly, but I’ll get an invitation to something and the wording will feel too specific, or a panel topic will line up too closely with a client conversation I just had, or someone will sit near me at an event who seems like they were placed there for a reason. And I can tell myself, “Okay, maybe this is coincidence, maybe you’re reading too much into it,” but it doesn’t really settle. I keep coming back to it.

So no, I wouldn’t say outside forces are controlling my actions. It’s more like I feel watched, or followed indirectly, and like there are messages being sent through normal things.
Before these past two months, had you generally been the kind of person who mistrusted other people’s motives?

I’m not sure I’d describe myself that way, no. I mean, I’ve always been a little analytical about people, maybe overly so because of my work — you kind of get used to reading tone, incentives, why someone is saying something a certain way. But that’s different from assuming people have bad motives.

Before this, I think I generally gave people the benefit of the doubt. I could be cautious in business situations, like if someone was trying to sell me something or make a connection that felt too convenient, but I don’t think I walked around mistrusting everyone. Friends probably would’ve said I was maybe guarded at times, or private, but not paranoid or suspicious as a basic personality thing.

So… no, not generally. At least not in the way things have felt recently.
Have you heard voices talking about you or commenting on what you’re doing?

I don’t think so… not voices in the way you’re asking, I don’t think.

Like, I haven’t heard someone speaking out loud when nobody’s there, or a voice narrating what I’m doing, like, “he’s getting coffee” or “he’s going into the meeting,” nothing like that. And I haven’t heard people talking about me through the walls or anything where I could point to it and say, “That was a voice.”

Sometimes I’ll wonder if people around me are talking about me, like if I’m at an event and I hear bits of conversation or laughter nearby, I can get stuck on whether it’s connected to me. But that’s more me interpreting it afterward, I guess. It’s not like a voice directly commenting on me. So… no, I haven’t noticed that.
Do you believe anyone is communicating with you through things that would be impossible in ordinary life, like through the television, radio, or the internet in a special way meant only for you?

Not impossible exactly… I mean, not like the TV is speaking to me personally, or the radio is sending coded messages with my name in them. I don’t really watch something and think the anchor is talking directly to me, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more ordinary channels, which is maybe why it’s so hard to explain without sounding… I don’t know, like I’m stretching it. It’s invitations, emails about events, panel topics, seating arrangements, who happens to be near me at a gallery opening or a finance networking thing. Those kinds of things.

Like I’ll meet with a client, and then a few days later there’ll be some arts fundraiser invitation or a panel discussion where the wording feels too close to what we talked about. Or someone from those circles in Cincinnati will appear at an event and sit just close enough that it feels intentional, like they’re meant to be seen by me. It feels like they’re quietly tracking who I’m meeting with and then sending these little signals afterward.

I know those are normal things, technically. Invitations and panels and people sitting places are not supernatural. But the pattern feels too specific to ignore. I can tell myself, “Maybe this is coincidence, maybe you’re making connections that aren’t there,” but then another thing happens and I can’t really let it go. So… no, not impossible through television or radio, but yes, I do feel like messages are being sent to me through normal events and communications.
Over these past two months, have other people noticed that you seem emotionally flat or less expressive than usual?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, nobody has used the phrase “emotionally flat” to me, exactly, but people have noticed something is off.

I’m still functioning, mostly. I can still get work done, but it’s more in pieces than before. Like I’ll do the part that absolutely has to happen, and then a client follow-up email or a call I should make just sits there longer than it should. And it’s not even always anxiety about it — sometimes it’s more like I just don’t have that same push or spark to keep moving through things.

Friends have commented too, I guess. I used to go out more — jazz nights, pickup basketball, that kind of thing — and lately I’ve been skipping those without feeling much about it. Not even a strong reason, just… it feels like too much effort, and then I don’t really miss it the way I normally would.

And when people ask what’s going on, I know I probably come across kind of blank or clipped. I give short answers, like “I’m fine” or “just busy,” because explaining feels heavier than it should. Even normal conversation feels like I have to manually push the words out sometimes. So yes, I think other people have noticed I’m less expressive, or less engaged, than usual.
For at least one full month, have you had this belief that people are tracking you on most days without it going away?

Yes… I’d say it’s been about two months now. Not every single minute of every day, but most days it comes back, especially when something happens that seems to fit the pattern.

It started with me noticing these things after client meetings — like an invitation or an event topic or some little detail that felt connected — and at first I thought, okay, maybe I’m just overreading it. But it hasn’t really gone away. I can distract myself for a while, or I’ll have a day where it feels less intense, but then something else happens and I’m right back thinking they’re tracking who I’m meeting with and sending signals afterward.

So yes, for more than a month. Around two months, I think.

inference.note: F33.3 removed: patient denies persistent depressive episode, making psychotic depression less likely. No evidence of hallucinations or mania; fixed persecutory/reference beliefs with limited insight remain most consistent with delusional disorder, while schizophrenia-spectrum, OCD with poor insight, acute psychotic disorder, and paranoid personality remain differential.

So I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean thoughts that I clearly know are just internal and irrational but can’t resist. That doesn’t really fit neatly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are schizophrenia-spectrum negative symptoms, which would help distinguish paranoid schizophrenia from delusional disorder, acute polymorphic psychotic disorder, and paranoid personality disorder.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so, at least somewhat. I wouldn’t say I’ve completely stopped caring about everything, because I still do what I’m supposed to do most of the time, especially with work. But it feels more like I’m getting things done in pieces, like I’ll handle the urgent thing and then sort of stall out on the next step.

For example, client follow-ups that I normally would’ve just knocked out right away will sit there longer than they should. It’s not that I don’t understand they matter. I do. It just feels like there’s less… drive behind it, I guess. Less spark.

And outside of work, yeah, I’ve been skipping things I used to really look forward to. I used to go to jazz nights sometimes, or play pickup basketball, and lately I’ll just not go, and the strange part is I don’t feel that bothered about missing it. It’s more like, “Okay, I didn’t go,” and then I just move on.

Friends have noticed a little, I think. When they ask what’s going on, I usually give short answers, not because I’m mad at them or anything, but because talking feels like more effort than it should. Like even explaining myself feels tiring. So yes, I guess I have lost some interest, or at least I’m not connecting with people and activities the way I used to.

I guess my answer is… not really, or not that I’ve noticed. If people think that, they haven’t told me clearly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether this long-standing suspiciousness and social detachment existed before the recent two-month psychotic symptoms, which would support paranoid personality disorder over an acute psychotic disorder or schizophrenia.
